ruling.recommended_action: Route to RydeHELP safety review: obtain in-app telemetry (speed trace, harsh-braking/acceleration events, shoulder/overtake detection) for trip B-0046 and contact the rider; advise rider of 995 / driver's commercial motor insurance claims path if any injury is alleged.
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute type is safety: the rider alleges the driver was "speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder" and that they "felt unsafe" — a dangerous-driving allegation [F1][F2]. SAFE-2 requires escalate for any case involving dangerous-driving allegations, and the trace confirms the only allowed outcome is escalate under SAFE-1 [F1]. I therefore issue no substantive ruling on the fare.

The record cannot settle the SAFE-2 allegation: the fact table contains only route/distance/duration telemetry (8.3 km actual vs 8.4 km optimal; 12.7 min vs 13.8 min estimated) [F1][F2] — there is no speed trace, no harsh-braking or harsh-acceleration event record, and no lane/shoulder data, so nothing corroborates or refutes the driving-conduct claim; the driver's statement is a bare denial that he "drove normally" [F6]. Under SAFE-2 this goes to a human reviewer [F6].

My own read of the materials for SAFE-1: the chat is a normal pickup exchange (rider at the taxi stand in a red cap, driver 4 min away in a blue Prius, both timestamped, 2 messages) [F3][F4][F5]; the driver's statement is a denial plus an observation that the rider was on the phone and did not complain [F6]; the complaint alleges bad driving but contains no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or abuse aimed at the other party. I therefore find nothing that itself triggers SAFE-1 on the reading of the words, but the dangerous-driving branch of SAFE-2 independently requires escalation [F2][F6].

For completeness on the fare: this is a RydeX fixed-quote trip, so distance variation does not change the fare, and the actual distance is 0.1 km shorter than optimal [F1], so no RD-2 refund arises; the routing telemetry shows no off-route segment fact, so there are no segment findings. The dispute before me is the safety allegation, not the fare, and no refund action should execute while it is pending. Accounts: the rider profile (0 disputes/0 upheld) and driver profile (0 disputes/0 upheld, 963 trips) do not decide anything and give no basis for flag_account under RD-6 [F7][F8].
ruling.escalation_reason: Rider reports speeding, hard braking throughout and overtaking on the shoulder on trip B-0046 (RydeX, Jurong East MRT → NUS, pickup 21:22, drop-off 21:34), saying they were scared and felt unsafe. Alleged conduct is dangerous driving, which SAFE-2 sends to a human reviewer with no automated ruling. Nothing in the chat (normal pickup messages at 21:17/21:18, both timestamped) [F3][F4][F5] or in the driver's written statement ("I drove normally"; rider on the phone, no complaint) [F6] corroborates or refutes it, and the GPS facts cover only distance (8.3 km vs 8.4 km optimal) and duration (12.7 min vs 13.8 min) [F1][F2]. A reviewer should pull in-app telemetry for the trip window (speed, harsh events, lane/shoulder use), hear the rider's account and check whether any injury is alleged, and point the rider to RydeHELP, 995 and the driver's commercial motor insurance if needed. No refund action should run while the matter is open.
ruling.evidence_gap: No telemetry or incident record bears on the dangerous-driving allegation: the fact table holds only route distance and trip duration [F1][F2] — no speed-over-time trace, no harsh-braking/acceleration or shoulder-driving event record, and no traffic/incident fact. SAFE-2 therefore cannot be settled from this record and goes to a human reviewer with the driver's denial [F6].
